Under the old system, almost every urgent order passed through a handful of capital hubs. Lose one station or one duty officer, and districts began waiting for confirmation that might never arrive. The Party will distribute transmitters, call-sign tables and copies of ciphers across independent communication posts.\n\nThis is not another radio station for speeches. It is a network in which capturing one office no longer means silence for the entire state.

For too long, the Bronze Congress has simultaneously been a symbol of power, an archive and the place from which the army expected its orders. A reserve headquarters will receive copies of maps, mobilisation lists, seals and communication channels in a separate protected building outside the government quarter.\n\nIf the capital comes under attack, the state will need not a monument to continuity, but a second desk whose occupants already know what to do.

We will arrange communications, documents and evacuation of the organisation in advance. Funds are evacuated through a separate decision; the plan does not transfer the army or the remaining state treasury.

Nodrul is fighting its own war. We will offer assistance and establish permanent links between departments. The agreement does not replace its decision on intervention; asylum guarantees are discussed in a separate protocol.
